title: Decision Trees — The Tree Memorizes Every Leaf
key_insight: Limit depth, require enough rows for a split, or prune weak branches. These controls trade a little training fit for steadier new-data behavior.
body:
## The Tree Memorizes Every Leaf

A tree keeps splitting until nearly every training row owns a private leaf. Training looks perfect, but tiny new changes send examples down brittle paths.

Limit depth, require enough rows for a split, or prune weak branches. These controls trade a little training fit for steadier new-data behavior.

Missing values and categories need a clear policy. Also inspect whether one high-cardinality feature wins simply because it offers many possible splits.
common_mistakes: Growing until every training row has its own leaf.
Reading one greedy split as the only valid explanation.
Ignoring the advantage given to features with many possible cut points.
mini_exercise: Draw the situation from “The Tree Memorizes Every Leaf” with three labeled steps, then explain what changes at each step.
real_world_usage: Trees handle curved rules and mixed features while remaining inspectable.
explain_back_prompt: Using the “The Tree Memorizes Every Leaf” story, explain Decision Trees without assuming the listener knows machine learning.
